brief: Throughout September an incrementally hawkish Fed priced in more hikes, while an oil price jump and competition for capital pushed real rates higher along the curve. This drove Russell 2000 down 4.2% for the month, lagging Nasdaq's 4.6% gain and the flat S&P 500. However funding dynamics richened: Russell 2000's 3-month funding versus Fed Funds rose 9bps, and its funding discount to the S&P narrowed to the tightest level since early February before reverting slightly. Commitment of Traders data for September 1-22 showed Non-Dealers net bought $3bn of Russell 2000 futures (Asset Managers +$2.2bn, Hedge Funds +$200mm, Non-Reportable +$560mm), possibly because Non-Dealer positioning started at a multiyear low on September 1. Alternatively, that support may fade: CDX High Yield hit roughly a 5-month high on September 30, and weekly Asset Manager short changes have historically correlated positively with CDX High Yield. The note does not resolve which read dominates.
